IRON.desc: A naturally occurring metal. High levels can cause rusty-colored water, metallic taste, and staining of laundry and fixtures.
IRON.source: Natural deposits, industrial waste, corroding pipes

NITRATE.desc: A nutrient that is dangerous at high levels, especially for infants. Can cause "blue baby syndrome," which reduces the blood's ability to carry oxygen.
NITRATE.source: Fertilizer runoff, septic systems, animal waste, natural deposits

NITRATE-NITRITE.desc: Combined measure of nitrate and nitrite, both of which can be harmful at high levels, especially for infants.
NITRATE-NITRITE.source: Fertilizer runoff, septic systems, animal waste

NITRITE.desc: Dangerous at high levels, especially for infants. Can interfere with the blood's ability to carry oxygen.
NITRITE.source: Fertilizer runoff, septic systems, water treatment

ARSENIC.desc: A toxic element linked to increased risk of cancer, skin damage, and circulatory problems with long-term exposure.
ARSENIC.source: Natural deposits, mining runoff, industrial waste

LEAD.desc: A toxic metal that accumulates in the body. Even low levels can harm brain development in children and cause kidney and blood pressure problems in adults.
LEAD.source: Old plumbing, lead service lines, solder, fixtures

COPPER, FREE.desc: An essential nutrient in small amounts, but high levels can cause stomach discomfort, nausea, and liver or kidney damage with long-term exposure.

CHROMIUM.desc: A metal found in natural deposits. Some forms are essential nutrients; others may increase cancer risk at high levels.

CHROMIUM, HEX.desc: A form of chromium linked to increased cancer risk when consumed over many years, even at low levels. The subject of the Erin Brockovich case.
CHROMIUM, HEX.source: Natural deposits, industrial discharge, power plants

FLUORIDE.desc: Added to water to prevent tooth decay. At levels above the safety limit, long-term exposure can cause bone disease and mottled teeth in children.
FLUORIDE.source: Water treatment additive, natural deposits, fertilizer discharge

TTHM.desc: Byproducts formed when chlorine used for disinfection reacts with organic matter. Long-term exposure may increase cancer risk.

TOTAL HALOACETIC ACIDS (HAA5).desc: A group of disinfection byproducts. Long-term exposure may increase cancer risk.

CHLOROFORM.desc: A disinfection byproduct and one of the four trihalomethanes. May increase cancer risk with long-term exposure.

BROMODICHLOROMETHANE.desc: A disinfection byproduct and one of the four trihalomethanes. May increase cancer risk with long-term exposure.

DIBROMOCHLOROMETHANE.desc: A disinfection byproduct and one of the four trihalomethanes. May increase cancer risk with long-term exposure.

BROMOFORM.desc: A disinfection byproduct and one of the four trihalomethanes. May increase cancer risk with long-term exposure.

DICHLOROACETIC ACID.desc: A disinfection byproduct in the haloacetic acids group. May increase cancer risk with long-term exposure.

TRICHLOROACETIC ACID.desc: A disinfection byproduct in the haloacetic acids group. May increase cancer risk with long-term exposure.

DIBROMOACETIC ACID.desc: A disinfection byproduct in the haloacetic acids group. May increase cancer risk with long-term exposure.

MONOBROMOACETIC ACID.desc: A disinfection byproduct in the haloacetic acids group.

MONOCHLOROACETIC ACID.desc: A disinfection byproduct in the haloacetic acids group.

MANGANESE.desc: A naturally occurring mineral. High levels can cause black or brown water discoloration and may affect the nervous system with long-term exposure.

ALUMINUM.desc: A common metal. High levels may cause discoloration of water. Research on health effects is ongoing.

BARIUM.desc: A metal that can cause difficulty breathing, increased blood pressure, and stomach irritation at high levels.
BARIUM.source: Natural deposits, drilling waste, metal refining

SELENIUM.desc: An essential trace nutrient, but toxic at high levels. Can cause hair and nail loss, numbness, and circulatory problems.

MERCURY.desc: A highly toxic metal. Can damage the kidneys and nervous system even at low levels of exposure.

CADMIUM.desc: A toxic metal that can cause kidney damage with long-term exposure.
CADMIUM.source: Galvanized pipe corrosion, natural deposits, industrial discharge

NICKEL.desc: A metal that can cause stomach problems at high levels. Some people may have skin reactions.
NICKEL.source: Natural deposits, industrial discharge, stainless steel

ZINC.desc: An essential trace mineral, but high levels can cause a metallic taste and stomach discomfort.
ZINC.source: Natural deposits, corroding galvanized pipes, industrial discharge

SILVER.desc: A metal used in water treatment. High levels can cause permanent bluish-gray discoloration of the skin (argyria).

ANTIMONY, TOTAL.desc: A metal that can cause nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea at high levels. Long-term exposure may increase cholesterol and decrease blood sugar.
ANTIMONY, TOTAL.source: Natural deposits, fire retardants, ceramics, electronics

COMBINED URANIUM.desc: A radioactive metal that can cause kidney damage with long-term exposure. Also a radiation risk.

GROSS ALPHA PARTICLE ACTIVITY.desc: A measure of total radioactivity in water. Elevated levels may indicate the presence of radium, uranium, or other radioactive materials and may increase cancer risk.

GROSS BETA PARTICLE ACTIVITY.desc: A measure of certain types of radioactivity in water. Elevated levels may increase cancer risk with long-term exposure.

RADIUM-226.desc: A naturally occurring radioactive element. Long-term exposure may increase the risk of bone cancer.

RADIUM-228.desc: A naturally occurring radioactive element. Long-term exposure may increase the risk of bone cancer.

COMBINED RADIUM (-226 & -228).desc: The sum of Radium-226 and Radium-228. Long-term exposure may increase the risk of bone cancer.

TRITIUM.desc: A radioactive form of hydrogen. At high levels, may increase cancer risk.

38-STRONTIUM-90.desc: A radioactive element that can accumulate in bones. Long-term exposure may increase the risk of bone cancer and leukemia.

RADON.desc: A naturally occurring radioactive gas. Mainly a risk when released from water during showering or cooking. Can increase lung cancer risk.
RADON.source: Natural deposits (decay of uranium in soil and rock)

PERCHLORATE.desc: A chemical that can interfere with thyroid function, which is critical for growth and development. Especially concerning for pregnant women and infants.
PERCHLORATE.source: Rocket fuel manufacturing, fireworks, flares, natural deposits

PERFLUOROCTANOIC ACID (PFOA).desc: A man-made "forever chemical" (PFAS) that doesn't break down in the environment. Linked to cancer, thyroid disease, immune effects, and developmental problems.
PERFLUOROCTANOIC ACID (PFOA).source: Nonstick coatings (Teflon), firefighting foam, industrial discharge

PERFLUOROCTANE SULFONIC ACID (PFOS).desc: A man-made "forever chemical" (PFAS) that persists in the body for years. Linked to cancer, immune system effects, thyroid problems, and developmental issues.
PERFLUOROCTANE SULFONIC ACID (PFOS).source: Firefighting foam, stain-resistant products, industrial discharge

PERFLUOROBUTANE SULFONIC ACID (PFBS).desc: A "forever chemical" (PFAS) that doesn't break down. May affect the thyroid, kidneys, and reproductive system.

PERFLUOROBUTANOIC ACID (PFBA).desc: A shorter-chain "forever chemical" (PFAS). Health effects still being studied, but may affect the thyroid and liver.

PERFLUOROHEXANE SULFONIC ACID (PFHxS).desc: A "forever chemical" (PFAS) linked to thyroid disease and immune system effects.

PERFLUOROHEXANOIC ACID (PFHXA).desc: A shorter-chain "forever chemical" (PFAS). Health effects still being studied.

PERFLUOROPENTANOIC ACID (PFPEA).desc: A shorter-chain "forever chemical" (PFAS). Health effects still being studied.

PERFLUOROPENTANESULFONIC ACID (PFPES).desc: A "forever chemical" (PFAS). Health effects still being studied.

PERFLUORONONANOIC ACID (PFNA).desc: A long-chain "forever chemical" (PFAS) linked to immune effects and possible cancer risk.

PERFLUORODECANOIC ACID (PFDA).desc: A long-chain "forever chemical" (PFAS). May affect the liver and immune system.

PERFLUOROHEPTANOIC ACID (PFHPA).desc: A "forever chemical" (PFAS). Health effects still being studied.

PERFLUOROHEPTANESULFONIC ACID (PFHPS).desc: A "forever chemical" (PFAS). Health effects still being studied.

PERFLUORODECANE SULFONIC ACID 8:2 FTS.desc: A "forever chemical" (PFAS) precursor. Can break down into other PFAS in the body.

PERFLUOROOCTANE SULFONIC ACID 6:2 FTS.desc: A "forever chemical" (PFAS) precursor. Can break down into other PFAS in the body.

PERFLUOROHEXANE SULFONIC ACID 4:2 FTS.desc: A "forever chemical" (PFAS) precursor. Can break down into other PFAS in the body.

PERFLUORODODECANOIC ACID (PFDOA).desc: A long-chain "forever chemical" (PFAS). May affect the liver.

PERFLUOROUNDECANOIC ACID (PFUNA).desc: A long-chain "forever chemical" (PFAS). Health effects still being studied.

HFPO-DA.desc: A replacement for PFOA, but itself a "forever chemical" (PFAS). May affect the liver, kidneys, and immune system.

ADONA.desc: A "forever chemical" (PFAS) used as a processing aid. Health effects still being studied.

PERFLUORO PFEESA.desc: A "forever chemical" (PFAS). Health effects still being studied.

PERFLUORO PFMBA.desc: A "forever chemical" (PFAS). Health effects still being studied.

11CL-PF3OUDS.desc: A "forever chemical" (PFAS). Health effects still being studied.

9CL-PF3ONS.desc: A "forever chemical" (PFAS). Health effects still being studied.

ADSORBABLE ORGANIC FLUORINE.desc: A screening measure for the total amount of PFAS and related fluorine-containing chemicals in water.

TETRACHLOROETHYLENE.desc: An industrial solvent linked to increased cancer risk and liver problems with long-term exposure.
TETRACHLOROETHYLENE.source: Dry cleaners, metal degreasing, industrial discharge

TRICHLOROETHYLENE.desc: An industrial solvent and known carcinogen. Can damage the liver, kidneys, and nervous system.
TRICHLOROETHYLENE.source: Metal degreasing, industrial discharge, waste sites

1,2-DIBROMO-3-CHLOROPROPANE.desc: A banned pesticide that persists in groundwater. Linked to increased cancer risk and male reproductive problems.

1,2,3-TRICHLOROPROPANE.desc: A toxic industrial chemical and contaminant from soil fumigants. A probable human carcinogen.

CARBON TETRACHLORIDE.desc: An industrial chemical linked to liver damage and cancer with long-term exposure.

DICHLOROMETHANE.desc: An industrial solvent that may increase cancer risk with long-term exposure.

1,1-DICHLOROETHYLENE.desc: An industrial chemical that can cause liver and kidney damage at high levels.

1,1-DICHLOROETHANE.desc: An industrial solvent that may affect the liver and nervous system.

1,2-DICHLOROETHANE.desc: An industrial chemical linked to increased cancer risk with long-term exposure.

1,2-DICHLOROPROPANE.desc: An industrial chemical linked to increased cancer risk.

CIS-1,2-DICHLOROETHYLENE.desc: A breakdown product of industrial solvents. Can cause liver and nervous system effects at high levels.

TRANS-1,2-DICHLOROETHYLENE.desc: A breakdown product of industrial solvents. Can cause liver effects at high levels.

1,1,1-TRICHLOROETHANE.desc: A former solvent now banned. Can affect the liver and nervous system at high levels.

1,1,2-TRICHLOROETHANE.desc: An industrial chemical that may increase cancer risk with long-term exposure.

1,1,1,2-TETRACHLOROETHANE.desc: An industrial solvent that may damage the liver.

BENZENE.desc: A known human carcinogen. Long-term exposure increases risk of leukemia.

TOLUENE.desc: An industrial solvent that can affect the nervous system and kidneys at high levels.

XYLENES, TOTAL.desc: Industrial solvents that can damage the liver and nervous system at high levels.

STYRENE.desc: A chemical used in plastics manufacturing. May affect the liver and nervous system at high levels.

1,2,4-TRIMETHYLBENZENE.desc: A petroleum-derived chemical. May cause dizziness and nervous system effects at high levels.

1,4-DIOXANE.desc: A likely human carcinogen that can contaminate groundwater. Difficult to remove with conventional treatment.

METHYL TERT-BUTYL ETHER.desc: A gasoline additive that can make water taste and smell bad at very low concentrations. Possible carcinogen.
METHYL TERT-BUTYL ETHER.source: Gasoline (fuel oxygenate), leaking underground storage tanks

ETHYLENE DIBROMIDE.desc: A banned pesticide and gasoline additive. A probable carcinogen that can damage the liver, stomach, and reproductive system.

CHLOROMETHANE.desc: A chemical that can affect the nervous system at high levels.

BROMOCHLOROMETHANE.desc: An industrial chemical and disinfection byproduct.

DICHLORODIFLUOROMETHANE.desc: A refrigerant chemical. May affect the heart and nervous system at high levels.

TRICHLOROFLUOROMETHANE.desc: A refrigerant chemical. May affect the nervous system at high levels.

ACETONE.desc: A common solvent. Generally low toxicity but may indicate industrial contamination at high levels.

METHYL ETHYL KETONE.desc: An industrial solvent that can affect the nervous system at high levels.

DI(2-ETHYLHEXYL) PHTHALATE.desc: A plasticizer that may cause liver problems and reproductive issues. A probable carcinogen.
DI(2-ETHYLHEXYL) PHTHALATE.source: PVC pipes and fittings, industrial discharge

DI-N-BUTYL PHTHALATE.desc: A plasticizer that may affect the reproductive system.

ASBESTOS.desc: A mineral fiber that increases the risk of certain cancers when inhaled or ingested over long periods.
ASBESTOS.source: Decay of asbestos cement water mains, natural deposits

CYANIDE.desc: A fast-acting toxic chemical that can cause nerve damage and thyroid problems at low chronic levels.

BROMATE.desc: A disinfection byproduct that may increase cancer risk with long-term exposure.

CHLORATE.desc: A disinfection byproduct that may affect thyroid function and red blood cells at high levels.

N-NITROSODIMETHYLAMINE.desc: A potent carcinogen, even at very low concentrations. Can damage the liver.
N-NITROSODIMETHYLAMINE.source: Byproduct of water treatment, rocket fuel, industrial discharge

N-NITROSODIETHYLAMINE (NDEA).desc: A potent carcinogen related to NDMA. Can damage the liver.
N-NITROSODIETHYLAMINE (NDEA).source: Byproduct of water treatment, industrial discharge

N-NITROSODI-N-BUTYLAMINE (NDBA).desc: A nitrosamine compound and probable carcinogen.
N-NITROSODI-N-BUTYLAMINE (NDBA).source: Byproduct of water treatment, industrial discharge

N-NITROSOMORPHOLINE (NMOR).desc: A nitrosamine compound and probable carcinogen.

SIMAZINE.desc: A herbicide that may affect hormone levels and is a possible carcinogen.
SIMAZINE.source: Herbicide runoff from farms and lawns

METOLACHLOR.desc: A widely used herbicide. Possible carcinogen with long-term exposure.

BROMACIL.desc: A herbicide. Limited evidence of health effects at low levels.

PARAQUAT.desc: A highly toxic herbicide. Extremely dangerous if ingested in concentrated form.

TDS.desc: A measure of all dissolved minerals in water. High levels can make water taste salty or bitter but aren't typically a health concern.
TDS.source: Natural deposits, road salt, agricultural runoff

CHLORIDE.desc: A naturally occurring mineral. High levels can make water taste salty and may corrode pipes.

SULFATE.desc: A naturally occurring mineral. Very high levels can have a laxative effect, especially for new consumers.

SODIUM.desc: A naturally occurring mineral. High sodium in drinking water may be a concern for people on sodium-restricted diets.
SODIUM.source: Natural deposits, road salt, water softeners

CALCIUM.desc: A naturally occurring mineral that contributes to water hardness. Not a health concern at typical levels.

MAGNESIUM.desc: A naturally occurring mineral that contributes to water hardness. Generally not a health concern.

POTASSIUM.desc: A naturally occurring mineral and essential nutrient. Not typically a health concern in drinking water.

HARDNESS, TOTAL (AS CACO3).desc: A measure of calcium and magnesium in water. Hard water isn't a health risk but can cause scale buildup in pipes and appliances.

ALKALINITY, TOTAL.desc: A measure of water's ability to neutralize acids. Affects taste and how well water treatment works. Not a direct health concern.

ALKALINITY, BICARBONATE.desc: A component of water alkalinity. Affects taste and water chemistry. Not a direct health concern.

ALKALINITY, CARBONATE.desc: A component of water alkalinity. Affects water chemistry. Not a direct health concern.

PH.desc: A measure of how acidic or basic water is (scale of 0-14, with 7 being neutral). Most drinking water is between 6.5 and 8.5.

PH, FIELD.desc: pH measured on-site at the water source, rather than in a lab.

CONDUCTIVITY @ 25 C UMHOS/CM.desc: A measure of water's ability to conduct electricity, which indicates total dissolved minerals. Not a direct health concern.

TURBIDITY.desc: A measure of water clarity. Cloudy water may indicate the presence of disease-causing organisms. Well-treated water should be clear.

TURBIDITY, FIELD.desc: Cloudiness measured on-site at the water source.

COLOR.desc: A measure of water discoloration. Colored water is usually an aesthetic issue, not a health concern, but may indicate other problems.
COLOR.source: Natural organic matter, metals, industrial discharge

ODOR.desc: A measure of how much water smells. Odorous water is usually an aesthetic issue but can indicate contamination.
ODOR.source: Algae, organic matter, chlorine, industrial discharge

FOAMING AGENTS (SURFACTANTS).desc: Chemicals that cause water to foam. Primarily an aesthetic concern.

AGGRESSIVE INDEX.desc: A measure of water's tendency to corrode pipes. Not a direct health concern but affects lead and copper levels.

LANGELIER INDEX (PH(S)).desc: Predicts whether water will deposit scale or corrode pipes. Not a direct health concern but important for water infrastructure.

LANGELIER INDEX AT SOURCE TEMP..desc: Predicts whether water will deposit scale or corrode pipes, measured at the source temperature.

TEMPERATURE (CENTIGRADE).desc: Temperature of the water sample. Not a health concern but affects taste and dissolved oxygen.

BORON, TOTAL.desc: A naturally occurring element. High levels may cause nausea and may affect reproductive health.

BROMIDE.desc: A naturally occurring chemical. Not directly harmful, but can form harmful disinfection byproducts when water is chlorinated.

STRONTIUM.desc: A naturally occurring mineral related to calcium. Very high levels may affect bone health.

VANADIUM, TOTAL.desc: A naturally occurring metal. Health effects at low levels are still being studied.

COBALT, TOTAL.desc: A trace metal and essential nutrient in very small amounts (as vitamin B12). Health effects of waterborne cobalt are still being studied.

LITHIUM, TOTAL.desc: A naturally occurring metal. Health effects at typical drinking water levels are still being studied.

MOLYBDENUM, TOTAL.desc: A trace metal and essential nutrient. Very high levels may affect the liver and kidneys.

SILICA.desc: A naturally occurring mineral (silicon dioxide). Not a health concern in drinking water at typical levels.

ORTHOPHOSPHATE.desc: A form of phosphorus sometimes added to water to prevent pipe corrosion. Not a health concern at treated levels.

PHOSPHATE, TOTAL.desc: A nutrient that supports algae growth in surface water. Not a direct health concern in drinking water.

NITROGEN-AMMONIA AS (N).desc: A form of nitrogen. Not a direct health concern at typical levels but may indicate sewage contamination.

TOTAL NITROGEN (AS N).desc: A measure of all nitrogen forms in water. Elevated levels may indicate contamination from sewage or fertilizer.

CARBON, TOTAL.desc: A measure of organic and inorganic carbon in water. Not a direct health concern but indicates overall water quality.

CARBON DIOXIDE.desc: A dissolved gas that affects water's pH and corrosiveness. Not a health concern.

SULFIDE.desc: Can cause a "rotten egg" smell. Primarily an aesthetic concern at low levels.

RESIDUE, NON FILTERABLE (TSS).desc: A measure of particles in water. High levels make water appear cloudy and may indicate treatment issues.
